Fatigue Risk Levels And Action Requirements

RISK LEVELACTION REQUIRED
EXTREME (16-25) HIGH (12-15) MEDIUM (8-11) LOW (4-7) MINIMAL (1-3)IMMEDIATE ACTION: Roster review required. Operations suspended until mitigated. URGENT ACTION: Senior management review. Implement additional controls within 48 hours. PLANNED ACTION: Review roster patterns. Implement fatigue countermeasures within 1 week. MONITOR: Continue monitoring, review at monthly safety meetings. ACCEPTABLE: No action required but continue observation.

Fatigue Countermeasures And Mitigations

ORGANIZATIONAL COUNTERMEASURES:

Fatigue management policy in place FRMS training for all personnel Roster planning software with fatigue logic Maximum shift duration limits Minimum rest period requirements Days off scheduling Overtime limits Regular roster reviews Fatigue reporting system confidential Safety culture supporting fatigue reporting

SCHEDULE-BASED COUNTERMEASURES:

Forward rotating shifts (day→evening→night) Adequate rest between shifts (minimum 12 hrs) Maximum consecutive night shifts (3-4) Recovery days after night shifts Strategic break scheduling Limited split shifts Predictable schedules Input from employees on rostering

INDIVIDUAL COUNTERMEASURES:

Sleep hygiene education Strategic napping before/after shifts Caffeine use guidance (timing/amount) Healthy eating habits Exercise recommendations Hydration awareness Recognizing personal fatigue signs Fit-for-duty self-assessment Commuting safety after night shifts Family/social support

OPERATIONAL COUNTERMEASURES:

Enhanced supervision during night shifts Buddy system for critical tasks Increased task rotation Additional breaks during high-risk periods Task simplification when fatigued Cross-checking procedures Controlled rest in flight (for flight crew) Check-in/check-out discussions
